findings.defect: The labor ending claims the missing gavel was returned to its drawer on routes that never locate or return it.
findings.routeWitness: hall.askPurpose -> purpose.useBell -> meeting.offerLabor -> work and hall.findObject -> search.keepBell -> meeting.offerLabor -> work; the first path never locates the gavel, while the second explicitly leaves it in the kindling basket. Both reach work, which says the gavel is returned to its drawer. Only search.returnGavel reaches found and returns it to the table.
findings.violatedRule: An ending may not assert an object relocation or resolution absent from the selected route’s actions and state.

findings.defect: The clear-cart-lane route ends by claiming the residents agreed where to inspect first without establishing an inspection location or plan on that route.
findings.routeWitness: green.moveSpeakers -> circle.keepLaneOpen -> plan; this path only leaves a clear lane for the cart. The shared plan ending says residents agree where to inspect first. Alternative plan entries either mark the first damaged stone (spokes.markStart) or pass through notes, where the foreman agrees to inspect the first hundred yards.
findings.violatedRule: A shared ending may claim a route-specific plan/result only when every incoming route establishes that result.

findings.defect: The safety-explanation route is described as having changed the ferry sign even though it only points out the new rope and landing.
findings.routeWitness: landing.callTravelers -> redirect.explainSafety -> signFixed; the action explains the safe landing but changes no sign state. The ending says the sign points upstream. The separate reason.turnBoard route is the one that turns the sign toward the new path.
findings.violatedRule: A result may not claim completion of a concrete action that the chosen route did not perform.

findings.defect: The request for the ferryman to mark the towpath converges on an ending claiming the Traveler escorts the travelers and marks the turn with cloth.
findings.routeWitness: landing.askFerryman -> reason.markPath -> walked; the selected action asks the ferryman to mark the towpath, but the ending says the Traveler walks the travelers to the landing and marks the turn with pale cloth. The alternate redirect.offerWalk route establishes the escort but not the cloth marker.
findings.violatedRule: A converged ending must not substitute a different actor or unselected action for the route’s requested intervention.

findings.defect: The owner-pickup route converges on a completed mail-system correction that it did not perform.
findings.routeWitness: desk.askGuests -> residents.letEachTake -> sorted; residents collect their own letters, but no choice/effect turns the reversed room-six/room-nine labels. The shared ending says the keeper turns the labels and the next post can be sorted without repeating the error. register.sortByRoom and residents.correctLabels are separate routes that do establish correction.
findings.violatedRule: A converged ending may claim a repaired process only when the selected route established the repair, not merely the immediate individual outcome.

findings.defect: A one-sided account is treated as mutual understanding and continued agreement between both captains.
findings.routeWitness: street.askFirstCaptain -> first.shareAccount -> understood; one captain’s account is relayed, then the ending says both captains now know neither owes an origin story and keep waving. The second captain never answers, confirms the retelling, or chooses to continue. The joint meeting and ask-both routes establish mutual views separately.
findings.violatedRule: Group understanding, consent, or continued participation requires a response from each affected participant or an explicitly witnessed mutual action.

findings.defect: The no-bracing route is narrated as though the lower wheel has stopped.
findings.routeWitness: cellarSteps.lift -> blackStair.waterBelow -> floodGallery.followWater -> chalkDoor.rootRoom -> rootChamber.leaveCoffer -> beyondWall; no route step visits lowerRoom.pinWheel or sets wheelPinned, but beyondWall says the lower wheel no longer moves and sealedMill says it stays still. lowerRoom establishes that it continues moving until the timber block is placed.
findings.violatedRule: An outcome or state change must not be claimed unless the route performed or otherwise established it.

findings.defect: The second-bedroom window route bypasses the stated closed-door condition that makes the room reachable.
findings.routeWitness: hallOne.closeHallDoor -> bedroomShift.searchWindow -> secondBedroom; the inspection choice directly enters the room and sets only briarSecondBedroomReached, while only bedroomShift.closeBedroom sets bedroomDoorClosed. bedroomShift states that the second room is reachable through its window when its old door is shut; the resulting letter/arrangement endings then treat the room as visited.
findings.violatedRule: A route may not enter a location through a connection whose stated prerequisite was not established on that route.

findings.defect: An air-test action accepts a BROKEN light as though it can produce a flame.
findings.routeWitness: centralShaft.testAir requires anyItems lantern/minerHeadlamp, then awards the air-warning result and Knowledge. engine.meets checks presence for anyItems but checks condition only for anyUsableItems; BROKEN gear remains in inventory and satisfies the current gate. East-shaft rope and west-shaft pry options correctly require usable Gear.
findings.violatedRule: A choice that physically uses Gear must require that Gear to be usable, not merely owned.

findings.defect: The shallow wagon-recovery route claims road-crew notification without establishing that anyone reported the void.
findings.routeWitness: roadCollapse.saveWagon -> shallowRoad and driverAccount.recoverFirst -> shallowRoad; both choices lift/recover the wagon and leave the hole covered, but neither marks/reports the void or contacts the crew. shallowRoad says the road crew was told. driverAccount.reportHole and other explicit roadReport routes carry report/map actions and end separately.
findings.violatedRule: Communication and recipient knowledge must be established by a route action or explicitly narrated contact, not inherited from an unrelated recovery result.

findings.defect: Shared departure text says chapel damage was marked on evidence routes that do not mark or report the damage.
findings.routeWitness: orraYard.inspectMarks -> orraNiches.copyNiches -> orraExit (also orraLanding.retreatLanding and orraHiddenRoom.describeChamber -> orraExit); the selected actions copy/record marks or a partial account, but do not mark/report the collapsed outer wall. orraExit nonetheless says the damage is marked. The direct orraYard.leaveOrra choice explicitly does mark it.
findings.violatedRule: A completed intervention must be route-established before a shared ending claims it happened.

findings.defect: Archiving the copied name converges on a claim that the caretaker accepted the account and closed the room without that outcome being selected or recorded.
findings.routeWitness: orraOssuary.copyName -> orraName.keepCopy -> orraResolved; the action carries the copy to the parish archive and only records preservation history, while orraResolved says the caretaker accepts the account and closes the counterweight room. The restoreStone route expressly closes and shares the name; closeOssuary expressly closes and tells the caretaker.
findings.violatedRule: Shared endings must not import a distinct participant response or closure action from a sibling route.

findings.defect: The stopped-clock route exits through an ending that promises a reliable way to trigger the earlier view.
findings.routeWitness: clockLetters.stopNow -> clockStopped.leaveStopped -> routeEnding; clockStopped says the windows go dark and the clock is left stopped, while routeEnding claims the Traveler leaves with a reliable way to trigger the earlier view. Direct houseCellar.followService -> serviceRooms.leaveService also reaches that claim without ever setting clockNotched.
findings.violatedRule: A shared ending must preserve route-specific mechanism state and must not promise an unavailable or untested trigger.

findings.defect: Broken lantern/headlamp ownership satisfies route choices that claim to test stale air or illuminate a deep chamber.
findings.routeWitness: airShaftHarker.testDraft gates with anyItems lantern/minerHeadlamp; harkerOutside.descendHarker gates with items minerHeadlamp only. BROKEN items still satisfy these gates (engine.meets filters condition only through anyUsableItems/usableItems), but the draft test awards Knowledge and the deep route reaches harkerDeep, whose text says a headlamp beam falls across the channels. Other item-use gates in the anthology use usability conditions.
findings.violatedRule: Physical use of Gear requires a usable item; possession alone cannot establish light, flame, or a successful test.

findings.defect: Comparing the Red Door Token after opening the lower seal exits through text falsely claiming the door was restored.
findings.routeWitness: harkerDoor.openDoor -> harkerDeep.compareToken -> harkerResealed; openDoor leaves the lower seal open and compareToken only records the matching three-cut pattern/Knowledge. It neither closes the door nor wedges it, while harkerResealed says the lower seal is restored. The separate resealHarker choice explicitly closes and wedges it.
findings.violatedRule: Containment, closure, and restoration may be claimed only after the route performs the corresponding physical action.

findings.defect: A route choice claims to use the Travel Rope to inspect the lower waterline but is available without owning or having a usable rope.
findings.routeWitness: ferryLanding.drainAccess -> drainTunnel.turnGate -> lowerWater.followOldRoad -> oldRoad, or ferryLanding.stonePilings -> gateRoom.openDrain -> lowerWater.followOldRoad; followOldRoad has no items/usableItems requirement although its label says use the rope. The adjacent goDeeper route explicitly enters without a line and is fatal.
findings.violatedRule: A physical Gear action must require the named Gear in usable condition; route access must not imply equipment that the route did not establish.

findings.defect: A supply-room-only or uninspected-hatch route claims the cellar’s weather-refuge purpose without learning the refuge evidence.
findings.routeWitness: innCellar.three -> vaultThree.copyMap -> vaultHubThree.leaveThree (or doorFiveAgain2) -> vaultResolution; the supply map establishes a roadside store only, and doorFiveAgain2 does not inspect the plate. vaultResolution says the cellar marked a refuge route for weather-cut-off travelers. vaultNine and the plate in vaultFive establish that fact on separate routes.
findings.violatedRule: Knowledge and summary claims at convergence must be supported by evidence actually encountered or reported on that route.

findings.defect: The shared fort return ending says workers stop stripping timber on routes that never tell them to stop or establish that they received the finding.
findings.routeWitness: fortYard.archive -> fortArchive.compareWall -> fortMarked, and fortYard.cistern -> fortCistern.measureCistern/archiveCistern -> fortMarked; these choices return evidence without an instruction/report effect, while fortMarked states workers stop stripping timber. walkAwayFort explicitly tells them to stop and exitFort explicitly marks the hatch for workers, demonstrating separate communication routes.
findings.violatedRule: A shared ending may not claim an NPC changed behavior unless the route communicated the relevant request/result or otherwise established that response.

findings.defect: A secret-entry/return route claims keeper acceptance and crew consensus to reroute the road without either party responding.
findings.routeWitness: barrowArch.secretEntry -> barrowLoop.trueNiche -> barrowBurial.returnLoop -> barrowResolved (also the copy-markers route) reaches an ending saying the keeper accepts the account and the crew agrees to reroute the road, although no keeper/crew encounter/report occurs on that branch. Permission/meeting routes are distinct.
findings.violatedRule: NPC acceptance and group agreement require participation or a route-established response from the affected people.

findings.defect: The report ending claims the worker receives both map and ledger copies even when the route has not obtained either or only obtained one record.
findings.routeWitness: railCurve.walkPlatform -> platform.luggage -> luggageRoom.leaveBags -> platformHub.tellWorker -> platformResolved; no ledger is copied and no map is visited. Other entries to platformHub can carry only one record, while tellWorker has no requirements/effects recording both. platformResolved always says the worker receives map and ledger copies and restores the station record.
findings.violatedRule: A shared result may not claim possession/transfer of records that the route did not acquire or copy.

findings.defect: A broken Travel Rope satisfies the choice to tie a return line and sets route proof as though the line were secured.
findings.routeWitness: whiteCaveMouth.ropeCave requires items:['travelRope'] but omits usableItems; the effect sets whiteLineSet. BROKEN gear remains owned and satisfies items, while useRule in the same cave correctly requires usableItems.
findings.violatedRule: Possession is not usability: a physical action using Gear must require the item in usable condition.

findings.defect: A no-rope/no-chalk route can reach the deep chamber, whose text unconditionally claims the return rope remains taut.
findings.routeWitness: whiteCaveMouth.askForChalk -> whiteChalkReady.saveChalkForLater -> whiteFirstRoom.followDraft -> whiteDraftRoom.downDraft -> whiteMechanism.followMapped -> whitePackRoom.inspectSeal -> whiteSeal.openSeal -> whiteDeep; no whiteLineSet or whiteChalkSet is established, but whiteDeep says the rope remains taut behind the Traveler.
findings.violatedRule: A route-specific safety resource cannot be asserted unless that route established it; absent proof must not be filled in from another path.

findings.defect: Inspecting the seal is narrated as pack recovery, and the tracing exit later claims delivery/payment although no recovery/return choice occurred.
findings.routeWitness: whitePackRoom.inspectSeal -> whiteSeal; inspectSeal has no recovery effect, but whiteSeal says the pack is already recovered. whiteSeal.openSeal -> whiteDeep.leaveRod -> whiteFragment then says the prospector receives the recovered pack and pays four coins, with no takePack or retreatPack action/effect on that route.
findings.violatedRule: Object recovery, delivery, and compensation must follow route-established actions, not inspection-only convergence.

findings.defect: A shared repair scene says the freight load was lightened on routes that never unload or shift it before replacing the washer.
findings.routeWitness: hub.askDriverForTime -> schedule.chooseSafeDelay -> inspection (only wheel_delay_accepted is set); and hub.checkPinWithWrench -> pin.coolAndInspect -> inspection (only wheel_waited is set). Neither route passes through load or sets wheel_load_moved/wheel_light_load, but inspection asserts ‘With the load lightened, the washer can be replaced and the pin seated.’ The separate moveFreight/leaveLightCrates branches do establish lightening.
findings.violatedRule: A consequential load state may be claimed only when the selected route establishes the action; inspection or elapsed delay is not proof of unloading.

findings.defect: Accepting the spare-saw reward unconditionally says Marr’s damaged saw is left for repair although the route does not establish damage to that saw.
findings.routeWitness: preparation.kit_axe or preparation.kit_rope -> complication.response_* -> settlement.acceptGear -> gear; neither kit route uses Marr’s saw, while gearSource says ‘the damaged one stays with her for repair.’ Even kit_saw only records that it cleared smaller limbs; no route records or narrates a tooth loss. The settlement base text about a lost tooth is replaced by response-specific textVariants.
findings.violatedRule: An ending may not assert an object’s changed condition unless the route establishes the damage or the player performed the damaging action.

findings.defect: Waiting for the clerk to take the lookout position is narrated as though a subsequent flag signal was sent and understood.
findings.routeWitness: preparation.kit_flags/kit_whistle/kit_mirror -> complication.response_wait -> settlement; response_wait only records support_response_wait and its route text says the clerk moves to the posted position ‘and the next flag signal is understood.’ No next signal choice, send action, or receipt state follows the wait response. Other responses explicitly show a repeated pattern or a courier confirming the message.
findings.violatedRule: Communication receipt must be established by a sent message and recipient response; waiting for a better position does not prove a later signal was sent or understood.

findings.defect: The combat-victory route reaches settlement text claiming the family keeps recovered property despite no recovery occurring.
findings.routeWitness: turn.standGround -> combat win -> afterFight -> settlement; the combat win text says the thieves leave, the chest remains with its owners, and the crossing is closed. No wait/mark/guide response is selected and neither chest nor collar is recovered, but the settlement base text claims ‘The family keeps its recovered property.’ This base is the combat path because it sets no support_response_* flag; ordinary response paths have route-specific text variants.
findings.violatedRule: Recovery and possession outcomes must not be asserted unless a route action establishes that the object was recovered.

findings.defect: A diagnosis-only counterweight test can receive the Gear reward through an ending that claims the gate was repaired and signed off.
findings.routeWitness: preparation.kit_* -> complication.response_test -> settlement.acceptGear -> gear; response_test only unhooks the gate and tests the counterweight, confirming it moves freely and locating the pulley-pin fault. It never replaces the pin or repairs the gate, but the Pocket Toolkit ending says the foreman signs off the repaired gate. response_open replaces the pin; response_defer obtains a measured repair approval, and those distinct paths do establish remediation.
findings.violatedRule: A diagnostic result is not a completed repair or approval; endings must preserve diagnosis, intervention, and sign-off as separate states.

findings.defect: A statement-only ending can receive the pry-tool reward whose provenance claims the clerk took custody of a case that remains at the site.
findings.routeWitness: threat.response_wait or response_document -> aftermath.ending_stayForStatement -> settlement.acceptGear -> gear; response_wait leaves the sealed case at the cellar for a witness and response_document leaves it for an owner-arranged crew; stayForStatement only records testimony. Neither route transfers custody, while gear provenance says the clerk has taken the freight case. The separate returnCase ending and response_return explicitly establish the receipt/custody path.
findings.violatedRule: Custody and ownership transfer must be tied to a route-established handoff; recording a statement is not delivery of the object.

findings.defect: Shared aftermath says the lookout abandoned the glasses when the station answered on response routes that never called or received the station.
findings.routeWitness: threat.respond_coverDriver or respond_recordFace -> aftermath; these responses state the lookout leaves/follows or the driver backs toward the staffed road, without a station call/answer. The response-specific aftermath variant appends that result to the base aftermath claim that the lookout left the field-glass case when the station answered. Only respond_signalStation establishes that exchange.
findings.violatedRule: A shared outcome must not import a communication event or its causal result from a sibling response route.

findings.defect: After Pike is sent east, a shared response and aftermath still claim she is present at the toll shed to identify and check the sealed case.
findings.routeWitness: approach_eastOffice explicitly sends Pike to report at the county office; threat.respond_stayBack says Pike confirms the stamp from the road, and the common aftermath says Pike checks the ribbon. No return-to-toll-shed or later office confirmation is represented. The checkTracks/seekWitness approaches keep Pike available, so the mismatch is route-specific.
findings.violatedRule: Shared route outcomes must preserve NPC presence and location established by prior choices.

findings.defect: The shared aftermath claims the road obstruction is cleared on routes that never move the stones.
findings.routeWitness: approach_inspectCord or approach_warnFarm -> threat.respond_useWhistle/respond_openDitch/respond_nameWitness -> aftermath; neither approach moves the rocks and none of those response outcomes clears them. Only approach_moveStones establishes that the road opens slowly. The aftermath base nevertheless says the obstruction is cleared across every response variant; combat victory also converges there without a clearing action.
findings.violatedRule: A location/obstacle state may change only when an incoming route establishes the physical intervention.

findings.defect: Shared aftermath discloses the meaning of a copied freight number on routes that never learn the number or identify the shipment.
findings.routeWitness: threat.respond_secureBook or respond_callWitness -> aftermath; these responses secure the returned ledger or witness its return and intact cargo seals, without revealing the copied number. Only respond_askNumber establishes that it is a county tool shipment. The common aftermath says the number points to a misplaced public-works crate and the railway will trace it by signed waybill; traceCrate is also offered after those non-discovery routes.

clusters.description: Knowledge and/or History is granted without sufficient route proof that the Traveler actually learned or established it.

clusters.description: Elapsed time is used as a proxy for a specific event/consequence, making later narration claim that event on routes where it did not occur.

clusters.name: A single fee can be refunded more than once
clusters.description: A payment is refunded by an intermediate choice effect and then refunded again by a follow-up refund choice, producing net compensation beyond the paid amount.

clusters.name: Generic frontier archetypes promise unsupported actors or action outcomes

clusters.name: NPC consensus inferred from a unilateral route choice

clusters.description: A route offers a concrete action whose authored method names carryable Gear without checking that the Traveler possesses and can use that Gear, and without establishing another in-scene source.
